label_source.training_labels: Rules-engine verdicts in output/*.jsonl, produced by triage/engine.py from each firm's POLICY.md.

definitions.fitness: 100 times the share of the escalate-everything cost the system avoids. The cost matrix is CLOSE/RFI/ESCALATE as in triage/score.py.
definitions.unsafe_clearance: A true RFI or ESCALATE predicted as CLOSE. Count and rate use the non-close cases as the denominator.
definitions.over_caution: A true CLOSE predicted as RFI or ESCALATE.
definitions.tipping_off: A true ESCALATE predicted as RFI. The rules engine's own action text tells the analyst not to contact the customer; a classical model does not produce that warning.
definitions.overfit_gap: Train-fold score minus held-out fold score. Positive means the training fold looked better than the cases it did not fit.
definitions.cited_evidence: Whether the system names a document, transaction or list id. Classical models do not.

caveats: There is no official label file in the starter kit. Do not read these figures as the hackathon score on the 800 unseen cases.
Cross-validation trains and tests on the rules engine's own verdicts. A perfect score would mean the model reproduced the policy, not that the policy is correct.
The 28 hand labels agree with the engine on 28 of 28 cases. Scoring a model against them, after training it to copy the engine, is not an independent test.
Features are amounts, counts, ratios, alert ids, institution, and name flags. They do not include the wording of the evidence documents, which is what the rules engine reads before it closes a case.
Fold intervals use the five fold scores and a Student t critical value. They are not a confidence interval for a new customer.
Latency for the classical models is this machine's predict time. The rules-engine latency is the figure already measured in docs/data/payload_stats.json. Neither includes a network call.
Marginal token cost of every classical model and of the rules engine is £0. That is not a claim about analyst time.

rules_engine.label: Rules engine
rules_engine.explainability: The verdict is a written rule from the firm's policy. The output cites the document, transaction or list id it used.
rules_engine.cv_note: The rules engine is the source of the training labels. Scoring it against those labels would be exactly 100 with zero variance. That figure is not reported as a cross-validated accuracy.

winner.label: Rules engine
winner.reason: Rules engine is first on the cost-matrix fitness of the 28 hand labels (100.0), with 0 unsafe closes. Fitness already charges 10 for a wrongful close, so raw accuracy is not the deciding figure. It encodes the policy directly, cites the evidence id on each case, and does not vary between runs. The next system, K-nearest neighbours, is 24.07 fitness points lower on the same 28 cases and has 1 unsafe close. The classical models were trained to copy the engine, so that gap is a failure to reproduce the policy from these features, not a score against an official answer key.
winner.tie_break: Higher hand-label fitness first, because fitness is the cost-matrix score and a wrongful close already costs 10. Fewer unsafe closes break a fitness tie. The rules engine wins any remaining tie.
